In the mathematical field of [[category theory]], an '''amnestic functor''' ''F''&nbsp;:&nbsp;''A''&nbsp;→&nbsp;''B'' is a [[functor]] for which an  ''A''-[[isomorphism]] ''&fnof;'' is an [[identity (mathematics)|identity]] whenever ''F&fnof;'' is an identity.

An example of a functor which is ''not'' amnestic is the forgetful functor '''Met'''<sub>c</sub>→'''Top''' from the category of [[metric space]]s with [[continuous function]]s for morphisms to the [[category of topological spaces]]. If <math>d_1</math> and <math>d_2</math> are [[equivalent metrics]] on a space <math>X</math> then <math>\operatorname{id}\colon(X, d_1)\to(X, d_2)</math> is an isomorphism that covers the identity, but is not an identity morphism (its domain and codomain are not equal).
